question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the DIPSI protocol from the IADPSG protocol for GDM screening?

answers.text: DIPSI uses a fasting 75 g glucose load; IADPSG uses a non-fasting 75 g glucose load

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is reversed. It is the DIPSI protocol that is non-fasting, making it more practical for low-resource settings.

answers.text: DIPSI uses a non-fasting 75 g glucose load with a 2-hour cut-off of ≥140 mg/dL; IADPSG uses a fasting 75 g load with three time-point values

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. DIPSI: single non-fasting 75 g OGTT, 2-hr plasma glucose ≥140 mg/dL = GDM (recommended by MoHFW India). IADPSG: fasting 75 g OGTT with fasting ≥92, 1-hr ≥180, 2-hr ≥153 mg/dL (one abnormal value suffices).

answers.text: Both protocols use the same fasting 75 g OGTT but differ only in the diagnostic cut-off values

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The protocols differ in the fasting requirement, not just cut-off values. DIPSI is non-fasting; IADPSG requires fasting.

answers.text: IADPSG requires all three time-point values to be abnormal to diagnose GDM; DIPSI requires only one

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: For IADPSG, ONE abnormal value among the three is sufficient to diagnose GDM; this choice overstates the diagnostic threshold.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key distinction: DIPSI is non-fasting (practical for India); IADPSG is fasting with three time-points. One abnormal IADPSG value suffices for GDM diagnosis.
Excellent. DIPSI = non-fasting 75 g 2-hr test (≥140 mg/dL). IADPSG = fasting 75 g with three cut-offs (fasting 92 / 1-hr 180 / 2-hr 153). Do not mix them up in examinations.
